title: Go-live Security Rapid Review and Exception Intake
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, rapid-review workbook for go-live security checks tied to RBAC v2, audit log schema alignment, SIEM export sanity, and evidence automation. Designed to support 15–30 minute security signoffs for lower-risk releases and to surface exceptions that require formal approval.

Scope & when to use:
- Use this for feature releases, infra changes, and model rollouts that touch auth, logging, or telemetry paths.
- Not a replacement for a full security review for high-risk projects (customer PII, regulated workloads, or new private deployment flows).

Quick checklist (pass/fail/needs-exception):
1) RBAC v2: role mapping and least privilege
   - Verify new routes/controllers have role annotations and tests (unit/integration).
   - Confirm new permissions are scoped to minimal resources (no global admin grants).
   - Check for any wildcard perms added to service accounts in this change.
   - Ensure Kubernetes RoleBindings/ClusterRoleBindings were created per policy and use subject lists, not broad groups.

2) Audit log schema and integrity
   - Confirm events emitted include required fields: actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp_iso8601, outcome, request_id, session_id (if applicable).
   - Verify new events are added to schema registry and have schema version bump.
   - Confirm no sensitive payloads (PII) are written to logs; if necessary, mask/redact at emit point.

3) SIEM export and realtime parsing
   - Ensure forwarder config has mapping for new event types; sample event forwarded to SIEM is present in test index.
   - Validate field names match SIEM parsers: e.g., "actor.id" -> "actor_id", "event.outcome" -> "outcome" (we expect the normalized mapping in the transform layer).
   - Run smoke queries in SIEM for the request_id to confirm end-to-end flow (application -> forwarder -> SIEM index).

4) Evidence automation & retention
   - Trigger evidence snapshot job and verify artifacts are created: policy doc hash, signed RBAC diff, sample log export, CI test run id.
   - Confirm automated evidence package includes hashes and timestamps and is uploaded to the evidence bucket with access controls.
   - Confirm retention policy applied matches the release class (standard 90 days for dev, 365 for prod-affecting changes unless otherwise specified).

5) Fallbacks & graceful degradation
   - Verify fallback model/route exists for inference endpoints when permission checks fail (avoid silent 500s).
   - Ensure alerts are in place for unusually high "auth_denied" rates post-deploy.

6) Exception triage (if something fails)
   - Low risk: add temporary allowlisted permission scoped to a ticket with expiration (7 days) + automated audit entry + post-mortem owner assigned.
   - Medium risk: require a 2-person exception approval (security engineer + product owner) and a compensating control (feature flag, additional audit sampling).
   - High risk: block go-live until mitigation or exec-level exception with legal signoff.

Evidence artifacts we expect to collect (automated where possible):
- RBAC diff (git commit id)
- Unit/integration test run id & summary (CI job link)
- Sample audit log event JSON(s) (redacted) with request_id annotated
- SIEM ingestion confirmation (index name + doc id)
- Evidence package checksum and storage path

Owner assignment template (fill before signoff):
- Release owner: [name]
- Security reviewer: [name]
- Evidence owner (automation): [name or pipeline id]
- Exception approver (if needed): [name]

Minimal signoff matrix (checkboxes):
- [ ] RBAC v2 verification complete
- [ ] Audit event fields validated
- [ ] SIEM ingestion smoke test green
- [ ] Evidence package generated and accessible
- [ ] Exception? If yes, exception ticket #[JIRA] and approver signed

SIEM quick queries (examples for security reviewer):
- Find sample by request_id: index=app-logs request_id=<<ID>> | head 5
- Count auth_denied by route last 1h: index=app-logs outcome=denied | stats count by resource_type
- Latency vs auth outcome: index=app-logs | stats avg(duration) by outcome

RBAC v2 sanity checks (developer-oriented):
- New roles added? yes/no. If yes, list roles and intended consumers.
- Are there automated tests asserting role->route access? link to test: <<CI link>>
- Any service accounts with cross-namespace bindings? If yes, justify and timestamp.

Exception approval guidance (recommended minimum):
- Exceptions must be time-boxed and attached to a JIRA ticket with: description, risk assessment, compensating controls, rollback criteria, and automated evidence hooks.
- Approval chain: security engineer -> product owner -> release owner. Medium/high risk require security manager approval.
- Record approval in the evidence package (approval name, timestamp, approval artifact link).

Rapid remediation playbook (if issues detected post-go-live):
1) Identify: triage using request_id, correlate in SIEM, capture first-failure event.
2) Contain: rollback or disable new route / toggle feature flag.
3) Mitigate: apply short-term compensating control (tighten perms, revoke token).
4) Recover: re-deploy fix + run evidence snapshot.
5) Review: 72-hour postmortem + update automated check to prevent recurrence.

Notes & gotchas observed in previous releases:
- Forwarder field mappings drift when teams add nested JSON fields; prefer flattened explicit fields for audit events.
- Tests often miss the downstream SIEM transform layer; include an end-to-end smoke step in the release CI.
- RBAC diffs should be machine-readable (YAML/JSON) to allow automated policy scans.

How to escalate this doc for a formal review (when rapid review finds red flags):
- Create JIRA ticket with security label and link to this doc + evidence package.
- Assign security reviewer and set 24–48h SLA for response for release-blocking items.
- For critical infra items, notify on-call security via #sec-oncall and tag the release owner in the ticket.

Appendix: common log fields we require for every audit event:
- request_id
- timestamp_iso8601
- actor_id / actor_type
- action (string, e.g., "model.deploy", "route.invoke")
- resource_type / resource_id
- outcome (success|denied|error)
